statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = 2, and the following holds. Let T be the undirected tree on vertices {0,...,n-1} with weighted edges {edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} of weight edges[i][2], rooted at 0. For vertices a and b, call a an ancestor of b if a lies on the unique simple path from 0 to b; the downward path from a to b is the unique path from a to b directed away from the root. Its length is the sum of its edge weights, with length 0 when a = b, and its node count is the number of its vertices. It is special if the values nums at its vertices are pairwise distinct. Then r[0] is the maximum length over all special downward paths, and r[1] is the minimum node count over all special downward paths whose length equals r[0].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 50000, len(edges) = n - 1, every edges[i] has length 3, for every i with 0 <= i < len(edges) the endpoints edges[i][0] and edges[i][1] lie in [0, n-1] and 1 <= edges[i][2] <= 1000, for every j with 0 <= j < n we have 0 <= nums[j] <= 50000, and the undirected graph on vertices {0,...,n-1} with edges (edges[i][0], edges[i][1]) is connected and acyclic, hence a tree.
